title: The Pattern Artifact may not be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas, regardless of token holder support
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 states the ceiling: "The Pattern Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

Three prohibitions are stacked, and the third is open-ended. Violating the Core Atlas and violating the Primitive specifications are checkable against text; "otherwise misaligned" is a residual clause that catches edits which are technically compliant but contrary to purpose — the letter-versus-spirit problem handled explicitly rather than left to interpretation at the point of dispute.

The structural claim is that a Prime Agent is a **subordinate jurisdiction**. It has its own token, its own electorate and its own amendment procedure, yet the range of reachable states is bounded from outside. This is what prevents the Agent layer from becoming a route around the Atlas: you cannot legislate at Agent level what you could not legislate at Sky level.

Enforcement placement matters as much as the rule. By assigning it to the Facilitator's *review* — the same step that gates the vote — the constraint is applied before any legitimacy accrues to the proposal. There is no scenario in the routine protocol where an approved-but-illegal edit exists and has to be undone; the conflict is resolved pre-vote or not at all.
description: Prime Agent governance is bounded rather than sovereign: the Operational Facilitator must enforce the ceiling at review, so even a unanimous PATTERN vote cannot authorize a misaligned edit.
